item.title: Major breakthrough into horror Florida jet crash that killed nine
item.description: Investigators have recovered the cockpit voice recorder from the Learjet 60 that crashed on 1 November near Greenacres, Florida, killing all nine people onboard, as the NTSB completes excavation work at the impact site
item.author: Tannur Anders

media:content.media:description: A dashcam captured the moment a private plane crashed next to a busy road in the Greenacres area of Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday, November 1. The footage shows the aircraft nosediving and exploding on impact as traffic passed by on Military Trail, between 10th Avenue North and Cresthaven Boulevard. The Palm Beach County Sheriff’s Office said Military Trail was closed to all traffic as authorities responded and investigated the crash. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said the crash involved a Learjet 60 carrying nine people that departed from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, according to local news outlet WFTV.
